_note: External MCP servers Talon connects to. Copy this file to config/mcp_servers.json (gitignored) and edit. Uses the Claude-Desktop format. Each connected server's tools appear to the tool-calling loop as mcp__<server>__<tool>, alongside Talon's own talents. Requirements: 'pip install mcp', tool_calling enabled in settings, and (for npx servers) Node installed. Remove a server's "disabled": true to turn it on.

filesystem._note: stdio server launched as a subprocess (needs Node/npx). Point the last arg at the directory you want to expose; subdirectories are included recursively and paths outside it are refused by the server. Tools: read_file, write_file, list_directory, search_files, directory_tree, etc.
filesystem._note_readonly: "readOnly": true registers only non-mutating tools, so write_file / edit_file / move_file / create_directory are never offered to the model and cannot be called. Use it whenever you only intend to read — server-filesystem has no read-only flag of its own. For finer control use "allowTools": [..] (whitelist) or "denyTools": [..] (blacklist) with bare tool names.
filesystem._note_search: search_files patterns are globs matched against paths relative to the root and are case-sensitive, so "resume" and "*.md" match nothing in subdirectories — use "**/*[Rr]esume*". directory_tree is usually the better discovery tool.

stdio_with_env._note: stdio server that needs secrets — pass them via env. Talon merges this over the process environment.

remote_http._note: Remote server over streamable HTTP. Provide a url instead of a command.
